correctness.rationale: Reconstructed independent side densities f_d(b)f_d(c), each f_d(s)=Gamma(d/2)/(sqrt(pi)Gamma((d-1)/2))*sin(s)^{d-2}, and independent tangent angle g_d(gamma)=Gamma((d-1)/2)/(sqrt(pi)Gamma((d-2)/2))*sin(gamma)^{d-3}. In b+c>pi, a0=2pi-b-c, delta=pi-gamma, cosine law gives 2pi-P=(sin b sin c)/(2 sin a0)*delta^2+o(delta^2). Cap probability is G_d/(d-2)*(2 eps sin a0/(sin b sin c))^{(d-2)/2}. Boundary sliver estimates plus integrability yield dominated convergence and Scheffe TV shape law; the three-phase Dyson/Selberg gamma integral yields C_d. For the mark, delta/r_eps produces density (d-2)t^{d-3} on [0,1] independent of shape. Independently evaluated coefficient C3=0.2423325195724113, C4=3/(4pi), C6=1/4; exact selected d3 coefficient agrees with earlier full theorem. Finite quadrature cannot certify tail or TV.

value.rationale: The nontrivial natural object is the near-maximal shortest-geodesic perimeter triangle of three iid uniform points on S^{d-1}, and the precise invariant is its all-dimension rare-event exponent/coefficient plus conditional circular Dyson shape and transverse mark. The variation of sphere dimension gives a genuine complete family of circular beta ensembles (including COE/CUE/CSE indices at d=4,6,10) and a dimension-dependent independent Beta(d-2,1) mark. The d=3 case is already published and should not count as a new contribution, but the all-dimensional law is a motivated structural probabilistic classification beyond that case and is not shown to be implied by known 2-sphere formulas.
